info.title: API.SH: Naver
info.description: The Naver API from API.SH: public Naver data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Places on Naver Map for a search (a place type and area, a name, an address): name, category, road and lot address, coordinates, phone, visitor rating and review counts, blog review count, amenities, booking and Naver Pay flags, image, saves and the Naver Map link. The first 50 places of the search.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/naver-place

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for, as typed into Naver Map.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Naver search results: title, link, source, display URL, snippet, thumbnail and sub-links for web results. `where` switches to the news, blog or Q&A (kin) tab, whose results carry title, link, source (press or blog name; none for Q&A), relative date, snippet and thumbnail (news also the Naver News link); the tab is echoed as `where`. `where=cafe` returns the cafe tab (post title, link, cafe name and link, date, snippet, thumbnail, reply previews; also at `/naver/v1/cafe`). `where=shopping` returns the products the shopping tab shows on its first page (organic, ad and catalog cards: name, link, image, price and discounted price, store, rating, reviews, purchases, delivery fee, category ids, ad flag) and the tab's filters; it has one page and takes no date options. `period`, or `from`/`to`, limits results by date and `sort=date` orders them newest first; the options used are echoed. Pass `next_page` back as `page`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/naver-search

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Pass `next_page` from the previous response; `next_page` is null on the last page.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: Search tab: web (default), news, blog, kin (Q&A), cafe or shopping.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Only results from the last: 1h, 1d, 1w, 1m, 3m, 6m or 1y (all = no limit).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD (instead of period).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (instead of period; default today).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Naver DataLab search trend: the relative search volume on Naver of up to 5 topics (each a keyword or a group of synonyms) per day, week or month, scaled so the highest point of all topics is 100, optionally for one device type, gender or age bands. Data from January 2016.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/naver-trends

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: Up to 5 topics, comma-separated; synonyms counted as one topic joined with | (the first is the topic name).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: First period: YYYY-MM-DD for daily points, YYYY-MM for weekly and monthly ones (a day is read as its month); default 12 months ago.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Last period, same form as start; default today.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
